title: Checkpoint atomic writes do not durably persist the rename
reasoning: The implementation fsyncs the temporary file and replaces the destination, but never fsyncs the parent directory. On POSIX, a crash or power loss can therefore lose the directory entry update even though `CheckpointStore` promises durable supervisor state, leaving recovery without its latest progress or proof.
recommendation: After `os.replace`, open the parent directory and fsync it on platforms that support directory descriptors; handle unsupported platforms explicitly.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests cover cleanup and command execution, not crash durability or directory synchronization of checkpoint writes.
suggestedRegressionTest: Mock descriptor operations and assert a successful atomic replacement fsyncs both the file and its parent directory.
minimumFixScope: Harden `atomic_write_text`; all JSON checkpoint and proof writes then inherit the fix.
